systems.title: The signalling systems the model tracks (a functional brain, not a cellular one)
systems.source: Standard neuropharmacology (Rang and Dale; Kandel): each system's main roles, and the caution that none is a single feeling. NEU-SYS. Each carries a tone (0 to 2, 1 = normal), a receptor sensitivity (0 to 2, 1 = normal; tolerance lowers it) and a time constant for sensitivity to return.

pk.title: Pharmacokinetics: how a dose becomes a concentration over time (one-compartment model)
pk.source: Standard one-compartment kinetics: C(t) rises with absorption (first-order, half-time ta) and falls by elimination (first-order with half-life t1/2, or zero-order for alcohol at about 0.015 g/dL per hour, Widmark). Alcohol: Widmark factor 0.68 men, 0.55 women; peak 30 to 90 minutes, slower with food (availability 66 to 71% after a meal). Caffeine half-life 3 to 6 hours; nicotine about 2 hours; theobromine 7 to 12 hours; morphine (laudanum) 2 to 4 hours; quinine (bark) 8 to 14 hours; mercury and lead accumulate over weeks to years. NEU-PK, NEU-ALC, NEU-CAF

circuits.title: Functional circuits: from system tones to outputs the rest of the family reads
circuits.source: A functional network, not neurons: each circuit reads the tones that drive it and emits one output on a 0 to 2 scale (1 = normal). The assignment of systems to circuits is textbook neuroscience simplified; the weights are the keeper's placeholders. Receptor activity is not behaviour (ChatGPT's caution, kept): every output is handed to an existing meter or attribute, never to a personality. NEU-CIRC
